open_points.subject: FlowEdge ordering in content_identity and prove_flow_version
open_points.text: “edges in the edge order of A05” and “edges, by (`to_node`, `to_port`, `from_node`, `from_port`)”
open_points.question: How are two edges with the same endpoints but different guards ordered, both for FlowVersion identity and for choosing the first proof failure?
options: Add guard port and guard value as deterministic tie-breakers
Order tied edges by their full canonical JSON
Refuse more than one edge with the same endpoints
open_points.default_guess: Order tied edges by their full canonical JSON after the stated endpoint fields.

open_points.subject: FlowConstant ordering in content_identity
open_points.text: “constants by (`to_node`, `to_port`)” while duplicate constants are kept and rejected only by proof phase 6
open_points.question: How are different constants targeting the same node and port ordered before hashing the order-free constants list?
options: Use the constant’s full canonical JSON as a tie-breaker
Include declared schema, class and value digest as tie-breakers
Refuse duplicate constant targets during composition
open_points.default_guess: Use the constant’s full canonical JSON as a tie-breaker.

open_points.subject: store.open_store startup cleanup
open_points.text: A18 requires that on start “value bytes no record names ... are removed”, while `store.open_store` says “The store's own temporary files ... are removed, and nothing else is” and no other State 5 operation removes unnamed value bytes.
open_points.question: Which startup operation removes content-addressed value bytes that no record names?
options: `store.open_store` removes both temporary files and unnamed value bytes
Add a separate startup cleanup operation
Unnamed value bytes are no longer removed
open_points.default_guess: Have `store.open_store` remove unnamed value bytes as required by A18 and State 4.

open_points.subject: store.spool_file ceiling refusal
open_points.text: The global convention says “A refusal is decided before the operation's first store change, so it writes nothing”, but `store.spool_file` says a ceiling refusal keeps “nothing ... of any file that attempt spooled before”.
open_points.question: Is deletion of files already spooled by earlier calls for the same attempt an allowed effect of a refusing `spool_file` call, or must cleanup be performed by a separate successful operation?
options: Make `spool_file` an explicit exception whose refusal atomically removes the attempt’s earlier files
Add a separate cleanup operation called after the refusal
Leave earlier files unnamed until normal spool removal
open_points.default_guess: Treat `spool_file` as an explicit exception and remove all files from that attempt on its ceiling refusal.

open_points.subject: installation.current_token_list after a failed re-read
open_points.text: “a failed re-read leaves no list until one passes” but re-reading is triggered only “when the file's digest changed or it cannot be read”
open_points.question: After the cached token list has become invalid, must every request retry the re-read even when the restored file has the same digest as the last valid file or the failed file has not changed?
options: Always re-read while there is no valid cached token list
Record the failed file digest and retry only after its bytes change
Restore the previous valid list when the file returns with its previous digest
open_points.default_guess: Always re-read while no valid token list is cached.

open_points.subject: Manifest api_base_url parsing and joining
open_points.text: An address is accepted when it is “an absolute `http` or `https` URL with a host”, and the request URL is “the `api_base_url` without a trailing `/` followed by the declared path. Nothing else is normalized.”
open_points.question: What URL grammar and joining rules apply to base URLs containing a path, multiple trailing slashes, user information, an IPv6 literal, percent escapes, a query or a fragment, and what exactly counts as a loopback host?
options: Define an RFC 3986 parser, reject user information/query/fragment, preserve a base path, and recognize only loopback IP literals
Use WHATWG URL parsing and resolution
Restrict `api_base_url` to scheme plus authority with no path, query, fragment or user information
open_points.default_guess: Use RFC 3986 parsing; reject user information, query and fragment; allow a base path; join after removing terminal slashes; and recognize loopback only from a parsed IP literal.

open_points.subject: service_invoker HTTP wire protocol
open_points.text: The request has exactly a `host` header, `content-length`, a status line and no client-added headers, but no HTTP version, ALPN policy or byte encoding for non-ASCII required-header and credential values is fixed.
open_points.question: Which HTTP version is sent, may TLS negotiate HTTP/2, and how are accepted Unicode header values serialized or refused so that the described request and the request actually sent are the same?
options: Force HTTP/1.1 and restrict header values to a defined ASCII field-value subset
Force HTTP/1.1 and encode permitted non-ASCII header values as UTF-8 bytes
Permit HTTP/2 with a separately defined mapping from `host` and other headers to HTTP/2 fields
open_points.default_guess: Force HTTP/1.1, disable HTTP/2 negotiation, and reject header values outside a defined visible-ASCII field-value subset.
